title: The Witch, the Dragon, and the Foggy Fog
markdown:
High in the northern peaks, ravines carved deep scars and mule paths zig-zagged like forgotten stitches, Witch Mabli kept a small observatory perched just above the trees. Wind sang lullabies; stars felt close enough to borrow. She was not a cackling sort. Sensible: socks mended, tea brewed properly, magic woven into the useful tense. Thimble, sleek black, silent as a good thought, missed nothing with emerald eyes and a tail that took minutes.

A chilly dawn wanted Moonpetal Parsley for a poultice—Sunstone Summit only, petals at first ray. Pearly fog had swallowed the range, a grey blanket with opinions. “A bother, Thimble. Even a clear day looks like a badger’s mood.”

Her map had come from a travelling sorcerer with a sparkly hat and too much flourish. Lines glowed. Every ravine and cave: technically correct. Emotionally, a chocolate teapot in a snowstorm—journeys of the heart, not the feet.

Satchel on. “Parsley still counts as adventure.” The map tried to knot itself. “Follow the Whispering Wind’s sigh north-east. The wind is sighing in committee.”

A voice like polished river stones: “Madam Witch? You seem a trifle perplexed.”

A young dragon hovered with manners that had been ironed. Sunrise scales, jewel-small shimmer. “Ignis. I have misplaced my usual path. The fog is disobliging. I am rather far from home.”

“Sunstone Summit. Herbs. This map prefers introspection to footwork.”

He peered. “Pathfinder’s Fancy. Interpretive. Philosophy over boots.”

They went, Mabli first, Ignis graceful. The parchment demanded giggling pebbles (loose scree) and a stream humming a forgotten tune (a trickle with no repertoire). Circles. Thimble mrrrowed, nudged her ear, stared at a faint game trail leftward in ferns.

“Not a prophecy,” Mabli said. “A shopping list with ambition.” She put the glow away. “The real way, Thimble.”

He hopped, stretched, trotted, tail a banner. Ignis offered, polite: “Clarity?” Warm golden breath—not fog, dragon kindness—softened the grey. A steep direct climb appeared like a sentence with punctuation.

Mabli chuckled, no whoooo. “More use than squiggles. Practical gift.”

They climbed: cat for truth, dragon for a nudge and a warming puff on nasty rock. Fog thinned. Summit, rose light, parsley unfurling moon-white among ancient stone. She gathered, deft. Sun on her face. Thanks, both ways.

With the land visible she looked at the map again. Not travel. A celestial chart: stars, alignments, a guide for looking up. “Patience,” she told it, and meant the sorcerer.

A simple charm lofted Ignis toward a clearer home-line. His thanks faded to a speck. Thimble purred a receipt against her leg. Home: poultice, kettle. She did not tell the trees. She labelled the parsley and left the Fancy on a hook for nights when the sky, not the path, was the problem.
characters: Mabli (witch Mabli), Thimble (cat Thimble), Ignis (a young dragon with impeccable manners)
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing mountain adventure fantasy for ages 9-10
author: StoryGen Community
